title: Company staff summit runbook and quickturn asks
body:
Purpose: Quick-turn runbook for the company staff summit (half-day) focused on Q2 OKR alignment, exec-level status updates, and a short demo block. This is a working doc — expect live edits during prep week. Use for coordination across product, infra, and GTM leads.

Top-line objectives for the event:
- Align on 3 company-level OKR candidates and the measurement plan.
- Surface top-two cross-org risks that require exec attention and decision.
- Provide a clear 90-day ask list for teams to pick up (owner + sync cadence).
- Rebuild trust on reliability/latency targets after recent peak-week incidents.

Event format (210 minutes):
1) 10m — Welcome & framing (CEO, Jen R.): why this summit, clear desired outcomes.
2) 25m — Exec state (each exec 5m tight): ops/infra, product, growth, finance. Use standardized 1-slide per exec (metric, trend, one ask).
3) 40m — OKR candidates (facilitated): present 3 candidate objectives, each with 2–3 key results. Live dot-vote to rank.
4) 20m — Breakouts (6 groups, 15m): rapid gap-mapping for top OKR, assign leads and draft milestones.
5) 25m — Reliability deep-dive (SRE + Serving runtime): incident summary, mitigations, SLA roadmap.
6) 20m — Demo block (product + research): 2x 8m demos, 4m buffer.
7) 30m — Decision session & wrap (execs): commit to OKR set, triage asks, publish timeline.
8) 10m — Close & next steps (People Ops): follow-ups, comms cadence.

Proposed company OKR candidates (draft):
Objective A: Deliver predictable inference economics for mid-market customers
- KR1: Reduce 95th-percentile latency for common generation paths by 20% vs baseline
- KR2: Lower hosted per-token cost for standard chat flows by 8% via batching/quantization profiles
- KR3: Sign 3 Dedicated pilot agreements with SLA commitments

Objective B: Make onboarding to Redwood Private < 10 days for enterprise proof-of-concept
- KR1: Publish a hardened installer + VPC quickstart with automated smoke tests
- KR2: Achieve first successful POC in two pilot customers (on-prem or VPC)
- KR3: Create a compliance checklist and runbook for SOC2/ISO handoff

Objective C: Improve developer visibility into model quality regressions
- KR1: Ship per-model regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets (10 repos integrated)
- KR2: Reduce MRM false-positive rate by 30% via labeled prompt datasets
- KR3: Publish public benchmark for top-5 open models with latency/cost bands

Risks to surface for execs:
- Risk: Peak-week capacity fragility — cause: suboptimal KV-cache invalidation patterns and burst autoscale lag. Impact: customer latency spikes, escalations. Mitigation (short): emergency autoscale script + pre-warm pools.
- Risk: Private deployment onboarding fails due to networking errors with customer's KMS. Impact: lost POC time. Mitigation: create a KMS troubleshooting flow and partnering checklist for SEs.

Open questions (to resolve in pre-summit prep):
- Which single metric will we use for "predictable inference economics"? (Options: cost-per-1k-tokens, median latency under 95th-percentile SLO, or a composite score.)
- Do we fold Dedicated sales commitments under the same revenue OKR or separate them as Strategic Deals?
- Can infra commit to a 6-week timeline for the 95th-percentile latency target or does that need 12 weeks?

Preparation checklist (owners):
- Event logistics (People Ops: Priya Patel) — AV, breakout rooms, streaming link.
- Slides from execs (Each exec) — one slide each, template live on Confluence. Due: 2026-02-22.
- Reliability summary (SRE: Owen Chen) — postmortem highlights + mitigations. Due: 2026-02-24.
- OKR candidate writeups (Product: Miguel Torres, Eng PMs) — drafts with measurement plan. Due: 2026-02-26.
- Demo readiness (Applied ML: Dana Li) — dry-run by 2026-02-28.

Communication plan:
- Pre-read sent 72h before (People Ops + CEO note). Include 2–3 minute video from CEO framing.
- Post-summit summary within 24h: one-pager + recording + editable decision log.

Post-event deliverables (owners and cadence):
- Publish final OKR slate + scorecard (Product Ops) — 48h post event.
- Weekly OKR syncs for 90 days (owners assigned in breakout).
- Incident remediation sprint plan (SRE) — 2-week sprint and weekly async updates.

Decision log template (for use during session):
- Decision title, owners, rationale, trade-offs, immediate actions, commit date.

Quick-turn asks (pull list for teams to start right after summit):
- Engineering: instrument 95th-percentile trace points for top-10 endpoints (owner: Samir N.).
- Product: finalize KR definitions and measurement query (owner: Miguel T.).
- SE/Customer Success: draft Dedicated pilot offering document (owner: Leah M.).
- SRE: build pre-warm pool helm chart and test harness (owner: Owen C.).

Backup/contingency options if time runs short:
- If exec state overruns, drop demo block and convert to async pilot videos.
- If breakouts need more time, convert decision session into a voting+async follow-up (48h).

Notes to facilitators:
- Keep each exec to the 5m template; stage a visible countdown.
- Use live dot-vote in Miro (link in linked_artifacts) and capture results immediately.
- Document disagreements as "callouts" with owner and date for follow-up.

Appendix: quick links and templates (internal):
- Exec slide template: https://confluence.redwood.internal/templates/exec-slide
- Decision log template: https://confluence.redwood.internal/templates/decision-log
- All-hands recording policy and transcript workflow: https://confluence.redwood.internal/policies/comm-recordings

Action items (right now):
- Miguel T.: push OKR drafts to linked Artifact Confluence page by 2026-02-21.
- Owen C.: scope pre-warm pool script and share a short runbook by 2026-02-23.
- Priya P.: confirm venue and AV by 2026-02-20.

This document is intentionally concise — treat it as a facilitator cheat-sheet. Expect iterative edits; flag any changes in the linked Slack thread.
